candidates.locator: Article I — Of Faith in the Holy Trinity
candidates.rationale: The Article predicates 'living' directly of the one true God as an eternal attribute of the Godhead itself, asserting the required proposition at full floor.
candidates.chunk_text: There is but one living and true God, everlasting, without body or parts, of infinite power, wisdom, and goodness; the maker and preserver of all things, both visible and invisible. And in unity of this Godhead there are three persons, of one substance, power, and eternity—the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost.

candidates.phrase: one true, holy and living God
candidates.rationale: The Confession asserts 'living' as an attribute of the one true God, the same subject and sense required, meeting the floor fully.
candidates.chunk_text: We believe in the one true, holy and living God, Eternal Spirit, who is Creator, Sovereign and Preserver of all things visible and invisible. He is infinite in power, wisdom, justice, goodness and love, and rules with gracious regard for the well-being and salvation of men, to the glory of his name. We believe the one God reveals himself as the Trinity: Father, Son and Holy Spirit, distinct but inseparable, eternally one in essence and power.

candidates.locator: Article 1. Faith in the Holy Trinity, ¶210
candidates.rationale: The Article asserts 'living' of the one God as Creator and Preserver, directly predicating intrinsic life of the required subject.
candidates.chunk_text: We believe in the one living and true God, both holy and loving, eternal, unlimited in power, wisdom and goodness, the Creator and Preserver of all things. Within this unity there are three persons of one essential nature, power and eternity — the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.
